SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Colonoscopy Report (fictional)
Date of service: October 29, 2026
Endoscopist: Marisol Quenby, MD (fictional)
Patient: Test Patient Arden (fictional) | MRN: SYN-55902
Indication: Referral for removal of a large cecal polyp seen on an outside colonoscopy.
Sedation: Moderate sedation with midazolam and fentanyl was administered by the endoscopist, with an independent
trained observer present; intraservice time 32 minutes.
Procedure
The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum and the terminal ileum was briefly intubated. In the cecum a 22 mm sessile
lesion was found. A submucosal injection of saline with methylene blue was made to lift the lesion, and the lesion was
removed en bloc by snare endoscopic mucosal resection. Two clips were placed prophylactically to close the resection
defect; there was no bleeding. Biopsy of the cecal lesion before resection was not performed.
In the descending colon a 10 mm sessile polyp was found. Removal with a cold snare was attempted, but the polyp could
not be captured and the snare removal was abandoned; the polyp was instead sampled with cold biopsy forceps.
No other lesions were seen. The examination was completed.
Impression
Cecal lesion removed by EMR with prophylactic clip closure. Descending colon polyp: snare removal unsuccessful;
biopsied.
Plan
Repeat colonoscopy in 3 months to inspect the EMR site and to remove the descending colon polyp.
Electronically signed by Marisol Quenby, MD (fictional), October 29, 2026
